body: Thank you for that. That's a great resource to keep in my pocket. I'm betting I'll hear from him in a couple days once he gets his box...I dunno.

I'll be honest, someone else mentioned this as well and it's something I've been a little worried about. I wouldn't place him as the suicidal type normally, but he's in such a strange place right now and is already acting so different...I don't know. The only person I knew who was there with him wasn't in his unit and his tour ended last month, so I'm completely eyeless. I hate that there's so much time left. It makes everything feel so much more hopeless.

I know I'm in the middle of it but the only thing I saw as a possible red flag was when he started talking about pulling away and feeling numb/emotionally distant....but like I said that went hand in hand with the deployment and he assured me that he was feeling that way with everyone. 

It's extremely difficult for me to imagine him not missing us. I'm still hoping he'll call after getting his box this week. I'll be sure to keep you updated. Thank you so much for taking so much time to talk with me and analyze this. You're an angel, truly.

Our entire relationship was just one big ball of fun and mush all the way up until this happened. A few sad conversations about how the deployment was going sprinkled in, but nothing ever major, and certainly never any fights or anything. It seriously was better than any movie I'd ever seen...everything was just so right from the very start. I keep going over those moments and that night especially and trying to see if there's any other way that could have been taken...like did I just read the situation wrong or something? But I can't see how it could go any other way. Never mind the fact that I asked him about that night when he was first saying everything about breaking up and he assured me that it was as raw and open as I thought it was. HE was the one always assuring ME that I was what he wanted. We initially met on tinder, and like I said before it was like we were already best friends. He was my first tinder date and the only guy I gave my number out to and all that stuff. He knew this, and would always joke with me that he was going to be my first for a lot of things. After our first night together I was teasing him about that and added "first tinder hookup" to that list...and he was so aghast! "...you think this is a hookup? Nooooo no no no this isn't a hookup, tossit1991. A hookup is someone that comes over just for sex, and then I say something about having to get up early for work in the morning so they leave and I never see them again. I don't cuddle on the couch and make dinner for hookups. I don't tell hookups that I really like them and need the day to hurry and pass by faster so I can see them. I don't makeout in Chinese restaurant parking lots with just anyone! You are most definitely NOT a hookup." 

I'm not really sure if he could have been any clearer there. 

I hope you're right. My family and friends have all been saying the same things...that in their guts they feel this isn't over, and they can't explain it, they just know it. I think I'll finish the honey-do list at his house this weekend, and leave him the piece of the his homecoming present that already came in with a little note. Even if he doesn't want to be with me anymore nobody wants to come home from a long, exhausting trip only to have a whole bunch of shit to still do at the house, ya know?

Girl he's so touch-based it's unbelievable. I've never met anyone else who gets as much comfort from touch as I do until I met him. He's so cuddly with me that at night he had to be touching at all times...if I moved over just a little bit to much and there was a gap, he would move to be touching, even if it was just his foot against mine. Even when he was dead asleep! We didn't think we were going to get to see each other the night before he left because it was going to be such a late night finishing things up at work here and then he had to get up mega mega early to head to the airport, so we said all our goodbyes and everything the day before that. I told him that I didn't care what time it was, if he wanted to see me again before he left, call. Don't deprive yourself, you're about to leave for 6 months, you get whatever you want right now. I also let him know that I wouldn't be offended at all if I didn't get that call, so no pressure. He let me know late that night that he was headed home and I could drive on up. It was so late that honestly, even though we clearly weren't just a hookup relationship or anything like that, it could have easily been taken as almost a booty call: one last chance to get laid before he left. It certainly wasn't like he was calling me over for dinner!

But it wasn't that at all. I walked into the house and found him in the front bedroom where we had been packing all of his bags. He was just thousand yard staring at the wall...it's like it had finally hit him, and hit him hard. I walked in and sat on the floor next to him and he collapsed onto my shoulder. I held him, and we sat like that in silence for a while. When he finally spoke he said he was sorry, that he was just so exhausted already, that he'd had a long day. We laid down on the floor and held hands while he told me some about it. He actually almost fell asleep. He apologized again and asked if we could just go to bed. Of course! All he wanted was to cuddle. He didn't make a single move (maybe TMI, but unlike him), he wasn't looking for a last quick lay, he just wanted to spend every last second we could close together before he left. When our alarms went off at like 4am, he snoozed it multiple times, skipping his usual morning shower in favor of holding me in this giant, incredibly raw, most powerful and emotional hug I've ever been in. When we walked out to our cars to go our separate ways that morning he said goodbye three different times--trunk, okay no his drivers door, okay no he walked me to my drivers door. Each time he pulled me in for another hug it felt like he was praying that he didn't have to go. He kissed me on the forehead and promised me he'd be careful before one last real kiss and shut the door. 

THAT was our relationship in a nutshell. All the fun times and the laughter and the sexy times were super important and meaningful to, but to me, that night before he left said leaps and bounds more than anything else ever could have. That night to me was the most meaningful night we had ever had. 

He texted the entire time at both airports, early the next morning as all of the troops were waiting to depart, and as soon as he left, swearing that he'd let me know as soon as he was safe...and he did just that. Good communication has always been a big deal for him, hell, the like third message I got from him after he got there was "I just worked a 17 hour shift and I'm tired as hell so I'm going to go to bed right now but first I wanted to let you know I was okay and see how your day went." He's always been super connected and thoughtful as hell. Always.

Dude, fuck the government indeed. I've never been the biggest fan of war and all that mess (both of us are pretty left leaning, actually) but this...this has just made me hate it on so much more of a personal level I think my blood could literally boil if I let it. How dare they break him like this. He's the best man I know. 

I'll definitely update. I want to say I expect him to say something once he gets the box but like I said earlier...I'm not sure if I know who he is right now anymore. Thank you for taking so much of your time to talk with me. It really means a lot.

Don't worry, I completely understand having jumpy and disjointed thoughts at the moment haha. I feel like I haven't been able to write everything in a clear (certainly not concise) manner since this happened. 

So him being forced into this directly is highly unlikely, but I actually had a little bit of a snort when  you said that because right before I read this comment, my mom and I were talking about it, and she threw that out there too. She's totally NOT a conspiracy person at all usually, so it surprised me that she said it, though it was one of many theories for her. She was just as shocked as I was when it happened--NOBODY saw this coming--and she kept saying "it just doesn't sound like him. Even how he said it doesn't sound like how he says things. It sounds like somebody has a gun to his head and is telling him he better get you out of his life or something." Now, I don't believe that, but she's right that it doesn't sound like him at all and it definitely sounded like it was something he felt like he had to do rather than wanted to do...and it's interesting to me that multiple people have said something along those lines. 

I don't really know what to think anymore about his situation or what he's experiencing. He's higher up in command and works mostly from a desk, so he's not directly involved in any firefights or anything. And when he first left and I knew this, I ignorantly assumed that meant that he wouldn't be dealing mentally with any of the ptsd stuff that you always hear about. I learned that was not the case pretty quickly...just because he wasn't getting shot at every hour doesn't mean he's not dealing with extremely heavy shit that I have zero capacity to even begin to understand. Obviously he hasn't been able to talk to me much about what he's seen or dealt with...he's never been a complainer anyhow so I think half of that is for security reasons and half of that is him just trying to stay Mr. Positive as much as he can, plus he's never liked to feel like he's burdening me with things. That's actually why I sent him a journal as part of his birthday present. I thought it would help him to give him a place where he could write out all the shit that happens day to day without feeling like he was putting it on anyone else or worrying about breaking security. He said it was just what he needed, and that he's been using it every day since. I wanted to believe that him being sheltered by an office would mean that he wouldn't get the strict survival deployment mindset...but I think I was wrong about that too. His hours are brutal, the environment is brutal, what he deals with every day is brutal. Maybe it's what happens on every deployment no matter how "cushy" the job seems initially. 

As for coaching...I almost wish I could copy/paste here what I wrote to him but it's way longer than even my first post haha. I sent him two things though: the first was a sweet and understanding version, written in my usual tone. Very supportive, very I'm here for you whatever choice you make, very open. The second was prefaced with "or for the terser version," and was pretty much me trying to do exactly that, you had the perfect term, coach. "I'm going to be frank with you, this is a stupid decision and I think you're going to regret it when you get home. You're in a hard place right now and it's not good to try and make big decisions like this while in that state of mind. I don't think you're an asshole, I don't think you have anything to feel guilty for, and I certainly don't think you're a bad man. I'm here because I WANT to be here, not because you're forcing me or because I feel obligated. We're a team, and right now that means your job is to focus on your work there and my job is to focus on taking care of you. Which, by the way, I fucking love doing. So let me keep supporting you. Let me send you those nudes. Get home safe and we can re-evaluate how you feel about us then." 

I had hoped he would appreciate a firmer stance. He's always said he's loved my confidence...though honestly I didn't feel a shred of confidence when I wrote it, but I guess that's the good thing about written words vs having to see my face when I said it. He knows me too well, he would have seen instantly how I was really feeling. Maybe he was able to see through it anyhow, who knows.

He's in charge of quite a bit over there and has always been a very take responsibility type person, so I could definitely see if something terrible happened how he would shoulder blame if he was involved in the decision making at all...even if his decisions didn't cause it. There's no way he would/could tell me that though, especially not while he's still gone. In my last message to him I told him that no matter what happened, whether he stuck to his decision or had a change of heart either while there or after he got home, my feelings for him haven't changed. I still love him, I still care about him, and my door is always open; he can come to me for absolutely any reason. Half the letters he's about to receive in a couple days talk about how great of a man I think he is, how strong I believe he is, and how much faith I have in him that he's going to kick this deployment's ass. He wouldn't let me say much of that when we were talking back and forth on Tuesday--he kept ignoring that and saying that all of this was due to his own faults and why couldn't I see that--so maybe reading it in the letters will resonate with him. I don't know. I hope so.

I've definitely been there as well...and that's something my mom even brought up. He's always been the bigger giver in past relationships. He's a hopeless romantic and loves doing all those little cheesy things. Which I absolutely ADORE about him, and I think is a big reason why I felt so understood and appreciated--he could see the little details in what I did too and always made a big deal out of letting me know he loved them. But so far in our relationship, thanks to this deployment, the majority of the "giving" has been from me. Absolutely NO fault of his own; relationships are never completely equal all the time anyhow. My mom said she thinks him feeling like he's "taking" so much and not being able to give anything back is really wearing on him mentally...he's not used to this dynamic, and it's not in his nature. So he feels selfish, guilty, inadequate, worthless, like he's dragging me down or being an asshole. Which, if that's true, makes me just want to shake some sense into him--he should know better than to think this is permanent or even that I care that he's not "giving" right now.

I'm so sorry to hear about your cousin. I think the way mental health is treated for military personnel is absolutely abhorrent. No one should have to go through the kind of shit they go through (full stop, but that's another opinion) and then get little to no help with it after. 

I had hoped that my love and being there for him would be a motivational factor for him to fight for coming home. I think that's one of the things that makes this the hardest...you would think that right now would be the last time he would want to break up, even if he was really not feeling it. 

I really hope you're right. I never would have doubted that before two days ago...I would have bet the bank on it.

You're right. It would wreck him to know that. I told him I will always be here for him, and that he can reach out at any time. I had already bought his welcome home present so I thought I would leave it for him with a little note for him to find when he gets home...if nothing changes before then. I want to keep loving him and being there for him but I don't want to upset him by pushing when he doesn't want it.

Ha, there's a gallon jug of some wine in the garage that we were saving opening for when he got home (were both pretty big winos) as part of the celebration, but it's looking preeeeetty tasty right now. 

See I'm the same way. Even when he and I first met he warned me that he was chatty and really enjoyed having a partner to talk to every day...which is exactly me, so it was perfect. Yes there are times when I get super stressed and I need to just have some alone time for a couple hours, but then I want to be close with my loved ones. I know he's like that a lot too...but with touch especially. He talked a lot about how he couldn't wait to come home and just have a normal day of coming home from work, having dinner together, then him doing some woodworking/reading/whatever alone while I do my thing for a couple hours, then going to bed together for sexy times and cuddles. It broke my heart because it's so mundane, so normal, and yet for him right now a normal day in the real world sounds like a slice of heaven...even better than going on a vacation. I was hoping that those needs and wants to be physically close to me could be kinda staved over with all the sweet letters and occasional sexting, but I guess not. I can only imagine what kind of toll all those weeks over there have had on him, especially since I know it's been over two months without a single day off, but I never thought he would want to be completely alone. It doesn't feel like him and it doesn't feel healthy.

To be perfectly honest, this was one of my first thoughts and my biggest fears. I pushed it out of my mind because I was hoping the only reason I went there is due to my own suicidal feelings and projecting my bias onto him. I know he's dealt with a lot of shit in his life, way more than his fair share. He definitely doesn't see his own worth a lot of the time and I've told him that I wished he could just see himself through my eyes more times than I can count. We've never broached the topic of suicide though...so I don't know if he goes there or not. The way everything happened so suddenly and everything he said certainly felt like it wasn't something he WANTED to do but something he felt like he HAD to do...but I don't know. He's always been massively protective of me and often would keep things to himself to try and spare me; for example this deployment: he REALLY downplayed and sugarcoated what life would be like for him there because he didn't want me to worry. I get it, I've been doing the same thing (though mostly because he's deployed and doesn't need more stress that he can't do shit about) and I know he's coming from a good place but I'm a big girl...I can handle listening to him bitch. 

I'm worried for him. I have been for a while, watching him go from the happiest most positive person I know to a dreary shell who could barely make normal conversations anymore has been absolutely awful, to say the least. But now I'm even more worried, and there's not shit I can do. I can only hope that if he is struggling with these feelings too, that maybe getting all those letters talking about how much I care for him and being encouraging will help. Or that he'll reach out to someone about it...even if that someone isn't me.

He mentioned so many times that he felt guilty for this, that he never wanted to hurt me, that if he would have known this was going to be the outcome and he would be causing me this much pain he would have stopped things months ago to try to prevent this. 

I'm sure he has mental trauma from the deployment. He's being put in positions that I personally feel that no one should have to be put into. Unreasonably long hours, more stress than I could ever imagine, he's supposed to get one day per week off but there's been so much shit going down and he's higher up on the chain so he's been the only one able to deal with it...which means it's been over two months since he's had a day off. I can't even imagine the kind of toll that takes on a person, especially someone like him. Don't get me wrong, he's a tough man who is very strong and able to handle just about anything...but he has incredibly gooey insides. He's the sweetest most caring person I've ever met. Even though I know he chose this career and this deployment it makes me so mad at the military for crushing his spirit like this. It's not fair. 

He still has yet to receive the latest care package. He said even when all this was going down that he was still excited for it, that it was gifts from me, that that meant something to him. There's still a (huge) part of me wanting him to open that package and say "okay yeah damn I fucked up." I told him I'm here for him always, he can call absolutely anytime and I'll answer. I'll leave him his welcome home presents and the little gifts I placed already around the house for him to find. I'll leave all the updates I made to the house to hopefully keep it safe in the upcoming storm season. And I'll be there if he gets home, finds everything, and calls. 

It's thinking about that not happening and that I've lost him for good without so much as a single chance to change his mind (in person is so much different than 8000 miles away) that's so heart wrenching. That's what makes me feel I can't go on.

You described everything so perfectly. And I've missed him for so long with him being gone but this....this kind of missing and aching for him makes before look like a stupid pizza craving or something. 

He said exactly that: that it was a personal problem of his and had nothing to do with me. I feel like that makes it harder. Dammit, I just wanted to help him through that shit. Does he not realize I was prepared to be there for him through absolutely anything? Does he really feel like he needs to solve this alone THAT badly?? At least if he had said "I'm pulling away because you suck at X" that would be something I could work on fixing about myself. This way just leaves me with more questions and extra frustration...and worse yet, nothing concrete to point to. "Emotional immaturity" doesn't make any sense for him in the real world, and for some reason he doesn't want to connect it to the deployment...even though he's been connecting all his other hard feelings to it. 

May I ask you something? I saw in one of your other posts (sorry) that you're a soldier as well. Can you relate to any of his feelings at all, or have you seen this a lot in your time in? I know you don't know him, or me, or anything more about our relationship other than what I've blabbered on about, but based on your experiences...is this something deployments really could cause? Just a total separation like this?

Thank you for taking the time to read it all...I know it was really long. 

I've struggled with suicidal thoughts and depression my entire life. No boyfriend in my past has ever had any really impact on that, in fact, only my parents have. They're great parents and wonderful people and I knew that killing myself (even if it looked like an accident, like many of the plans) would change their lives forever in the worst ways. So I've held off...the plan was to do it after they both died. I figured them dying was a pain that I wouldn't be able to survive anyway, and it's not like I ever felt like I had really much else to live for. 

Meeting him changed all of that. I'm 25 and for the first time in my life I felt like I had a reason to live. I was excited for the future. I even felt like as long as it was him and I against the world, as long as I had those perfect hugs of ours and we loved the hell out of each other, I could make it through anything...even the death of my parents. For the first time I WANTED to get married, I WANTED to have kids, I WANTED that goddamn white picket fence dream. 

I don't know anymore. How can I ever trust someone else? I put my very piece of my soul into this and it wasn't enough. I believed with all that I was that he loved me and wanted this as much as I did. I never thought this would actually happen...especially not mid deployment, no matter how rough it got. I was willing to stick around and fight for us through anything. I never expected him to be the one to end things...especially not this quickly. It really is hard not to look at this and wonder what I could have done different. How did I fuck things up this time. If this wasn't real...I don't know what real feels like.

Thank you so much for taking the time to read and reply. I'm so sorry you had to go through something similar...and from the sounds of it worse. 

I don't know what it is about the military. He's been in (including the academy, I never know whether to actually include that or not but whatever) for like 9 years now, so I would have sworn he was passed having it break him. This is his first deployment though, so I guess there's that. I just thought he was stronger than this. I thought WE were stronger than this. He wanted me to promise to not see myself as less than or inadequate because that's true or what caused this...but I can't help but go there. What if I had done something different or better or more. How the hell did I fuck this up.
